items.title: Islanders place Kyle Palmieri on injured reserve, recall Calum Ritchie
items.summary: The New York Islanders placed winger Kyle Palmieri on injured reserve and recalled centre Calum Ritchie from the AHL’s Hamilton Hammers.
items.body: The New York Islanders placed winger Kyle Palmieri on injured reserve and recalled centre Calum Ritchie from the AHL's Hamilton Hammers, the NHL club announced Tuesday. Palmieri was injured during Monday's loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs. He sustained a lower-body injury after getting tangled with Leafs players near the net and taking an awkward fall toward the goal. He logged 8:12 of ice time before being removed for the rest of the game. There's no timeline on Palmieri's return. He has nine points in 23 contests at the time of the injury. Despite registering 30 points in his 65-game rookie season, 2023 first-round pick Ritchie has only recorded two points in eight games of action so far this season.

items.title: Blues issue injury updates for four players
items.summary: The Blues are 13-9-2 with 28 points and currently hold the second Wildcard spot in the West.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Connor Hamilton-Imagn Images The St. Louis Blues announced several injury updates for multiple players Tuesday. Forward Connor McMichael and defenseman Brandon Carlo were both placed on injured reserve with lower-body injuries. The Blues also announced that forwards Jimmy Snuggerud and Pavel Buchnevich were both day-to-day with upper-body injuries. According to a news release, St. Louis recalled forward Otto Stenberg and defenseman Adam Jiricek from the Springfield Thunderbirds, their AHL affiliate. McMichael has three goals and eight assists for 11 points in 22 games this season. Meanwhile, Carlo has a goal and three assists for four points while averaging 17:43 of ice time in 24 games. Snuggerud, 22, he leads the team with 14 goals. He also has six assists for a combined 20 points, which ranks second on the team behind forward Robert Thomas and his 24 points. As for Buchnevich, he has six goals and five assists for 11 points in 23 games. Stenberg, a 2023 first-round pick, has three goals and three assists for six points in 15 AHL games this season. As for Jiricek, the 2024 first rounder has one goal and two assists for three points in 17 games with the Blues, as well as four assists in five games with the AHL’s Thunderbirds. Going into Tuesday night, St. Louis is 13-9-2 with 28 points through their first 24 games of the 2026-27 regular season. They rank fifth in the Central Division and hold the second Wildcard spot in the Western Conference . The Blues’ next game is Wednesday on the road against the New York Islanders . They close out the week with two home games against the Dallas Stars and Washington Capitals .

items.title: What The NHL's U.S. Thanksgiving Checkpoint Teaches Us About The 2026-27 Season
items.summary: U.S. Thanksgiving has traditionally served as a measuring stick for where each NHL team's competitive outlook for the season stands. Could this year be an outlier?
items.body: Nov 24, 2026 10:56 PM Published Nov 24, 2026 10:56 PM Updated Nov 24, 2026 10:57 PM U.S. Thanksgiving has traditionally served as a measuring stick for where each NHL team's competitive outlook for the season stands. Could this year be an outlier? There are multiple checkpoints throughout each NHL season where teams assess their competitive hopes, and U.S. Thanksgiving is traditionally a very important one. Every team has just recently passed the first quarter of the regular season, and there's still a ton of hockey to be played. But as history shows, this point in the calendar typically dictates a lot of what we'll see throughout the rest of the year. So what makes U.S. Thanksgiving such an important part of the NHL calendar? Over the past five seasons, 11 of the 16 teams who qualify for the Stanley Cup playoffs were in post-season positions at American Thanksgiving. Going back even further, an average of 12.28 teams in playoff spots at this benchmark since the 2005-06 season have ended up in the post-season (excluding the 2012-13 lockout, along with the shortened 2020 and 2021 seasons. That's a nearly 20-year sample size with almost 77 percent accuracy. That safety list should probably also include historically high-end teams who have banked points early on in weaker divisions like the Vegas Golden Knights and the New Jersey Devils . The Maple Leafs’ active roster now stands at 21. Tverberg, 24, has been with the Maple Leafs for the past two weeks. The former seventh-round pick had an uneventful recall, going scoreless in seven contests with a -4 rating, while averaging 11:24 of ice time per game. During his call-up, Tverberg spent most of his time alongside John Tavares and William Nylander . The line combination didn’t prove fruitful, as the trio produced a 36.7% xGoals%, according to MoneyPuck . Furthermore, Toronto had lost every game with Tverberg on the roster until yesterday evening, when they defeated the New York Islanders. In his eight career appearances with the Maple Leafs, the only win he’s been a part of was against the Islanders. Meanwhile, like Tverberg, Brisson has spent much of the past two weeks with the Maple Leafs after being recalled on November 12th. Still, unlike Tverberg, he did not play. After clearing waivers before the season, Brisson can spend 18 more days with Toronto before he becomes waiver-eligible again. Although he hasn’t appeared in an NHL contest with Toronto, he’s having a good season by all accounts. In the AHL, with the Marlies, Brisson has registered eight goals and 17 points in 14 games with a -2 rating. Last season, the former first-round pick scored 19 goals and 37 points in 66 games with the Hartford Wolf Pack.

items.body: Register Login Panthers Place Cole Schwindt On Waivers By Brennan McClain | at November 24, 2026 2:37 pm A day after losing forward Cole Reinhardt on waivers to the Vancouver Canucks, the Florida Panthers are exposing another forward to the other 31 teams. According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman , the Panthers have placed Cole Schwindt on waivers. As much as it would hurt to lose two forwards in a matter of days, Florida is expected to return Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand for tomorrow’s contest against the Ottawa Senators. With respect to Reinhardt and Schwindt, the Panthers would comfortably make that swap 11 out of 10 times. Like Reinhardt, Schwindt made his way to Florida via waivers. The Panthers claimed the bottom-six forward a few days before the puck dropped in the 2025-26 season. He spent the entire regular season with Florida, scoring five goals and seven points in 29 games with a +2 rating. He also displayed decent physicality by blocking 11 shots and delivering 39 hits. This year, aside from a five-game stretch with the Charlotte Checkers in the AHL, Schwindt has again featured with the Panthers. Unfortunately, he hasn’t been productive, going scoreless in 15 appearances with a -5 rating, while averaging 8:28 of ice time per game. Still, he looked good with the Checkers, registering one goal and three points. If he clears waivers, unlike Reinhardt, the Panthers will likely assign Schwindt back to Charlotte. Still, he’s signed through next season at a league minimum salary, and a forward-needy team might be interested in him.

items.title: Islanders place Kyle Palmieri on injured reserve
items.summary: Palmieri left Monday’s 4-2 loss to the Leafs with a lower-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The New York Islanders have finally provided a status for Kyle Palmieri, as the winger was placed on injured reserve earlier on Tuesday. This transaction comes in the wake of Monday’s 4-2 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs , where Palmieri sustained a lower-body injury in the second period after an awkward fall caused him to fall into the Islanders net. He left the game shortly after, and was announced as out for the rest of the game ahead of the third period. Palmieri’s status was unknown to start Tuesday, as even when the Islanders held a practice, no update was provided on him other than that he was seeing the doctor that day to get a proper prognosis. While the Islanders have yet to make a formal announcement of Palmieri’s timeline for return, an IR placement at least confirms that he will miss at least the next seven days with his injury, as he is not allowed to be activated off of IR within that time. The Islanders play three games within the next seven days. At this point in time, no other roster moves have been made in response to Palmieri’s IR placement. Palmieri has had a slow start to the season by his standards, as he has just four goals and five assists for nine points in 23 games . It’s the worst scoring pace of his career since establishing himself as an NHL regular in 2013, although it should be expected for a player who is now 35 years old. With Palmieri out of the lineup, Mathew Barzal is expected to replace the Smithtown, New York product on the top line alongside Bo Horvat and Simon Holmstrom. In the last three seasons, this trio has held the score even at 3-3 and has a 36.18% 5v5 expected goal share in 58:49 of ice time, according to Natural Stat Trick . Mitchell Chaffee is expected to draw into the lineup in place of Palmieri.

items.title: Can Michael Hage Become For The Red Wings What Jarome Iginla Was For The Flames?
items.summary: Michael Hage has the potential to be the kind of player who will make the Detroit Red Wings forget about Dylan Larkin.
items.body: Nov 24, 2026 8:15 PM Published Nov 24, 2026 8:15 PM Michael Hage has the potential to be the kind of player who will make the Detroit Red Wings forget about Dylan Larkin. Montreal Canadiens GM Kent Hughes knows he's giving up a great young player and NHL prospect in Michael Hage in the Dylan Larkin trade. But this is precisely why the previously bottom-feeder Canadiens have been stockpiling prospects over the years. Either Hage was going to come in and be a very good player for them or the Canadiens were going to use him to acquire a piece they need now . Hage, who was the ninth best NHL-affiliated propsect in this year's THN Future Watch edition, has the potential to be that kind of player. Someone who will make the Detroit Red Wings forget about Dylan Larkin. The trade that comes to mind for me is in 1995 when the Dallas Stars did just what the Canadiens are doing now. They dealt away a top prospect named Jarome Iginla to get Joe Nieuwendyk in a blockbuster deal. Nieuwendyk went on to help deliver the Stars their only Stanley Cup, while Iginla went on to forge a Hall of Fame career with the Calgary Flames .

items.title: Travis Green a major factor in Senators overcoming Brady Tkachuk trade
items.summary: Steve Peters joined Daily Faceoff Live to talk about the Senators and how Green has helped their success this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn A lot of people counted out the Ottawa Senators after Brady Tkachuk’s trade request forced a move to the Florida Panthers , especially when it felt like the Sens didn’t get a player of a similar calibre to their former captain. And yet, almost two months into the season and the Senators sit atop the Atlantic Division with a 16-6-3 record , and could be the class of the toughest division in the league. A lot of that success should be credited to head coach Travis Green, who is getting Ottawa to play to the sum of their parts to compensate for the talent they lost in Tkachuk. Steve Peters joined Daily Faceoff Live to talk about the Senators and how Green has helped their success this season. Steve Peters: When I make mistakes or say something foolish, I’m going to come back and tell you. I thought this was going to be a difficult start for the Ottawa Senators losing Brady Tkachuk. items.body: Register Login Wild Place Calvin Pickard On Waivers By Gabriel Foley | at November 24, 2026 1:27 pm Following Filip Gustavsson ’s season debut on Monday, the Minnesota Wild have placed third-string goaltender Calvin Pickard on waivers. This will solidify Minnesota’s goaltending duo after Gustavsson recovered from his offseason hip surgery. Pickard appeared in three games while serving as backup to Jesper Wallstedt through the start of the season. He set a 1-1-1 record with a .855 save percentage and 3.60 goals-against-average. Minnesota signed Pickard to a one-year, $1MM contract over the summer. That deal will maintain his $1MM salary through an assignment to the minor-leagues – a small perk for the veteran of 15 pro seasons. Across his career, Pickard has recorded a 161-117-40 record and .913 save percentage in 329 AHL games. He has also set a 75-78-15 record and .900 save percentage in 194 NHL games. Now 34 years old, he brings the leadership of a seasoned pro to Minnesota’s depth chart. A seven-figure salary will likely prevent any teams from claiming Pickard, setting him up for a second-straight season of AHL minutes. Pickard could take over an Iowa Wild crease that has been split between Riley Mercer and William Rousseau . The two have nearly identical stat lines – with Mercer setting a 3-5-2 record and .900 save percentage in 10 games while Rousseau has a 3-5-1 record and .899 save percentage in nine games. Notably, Rousseau is on an AHL contract, which could make him the most expendable option in a room with two other goalies on NHL deals. Rousseau could even be a candidate for a move to the ECHL, though it’ll be to a new team after the Iowa Heartlanders folded over the summer. Minnesota is now affiliated with the Jacksonville Icemen.

items.summary: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins missed the last five games with injury. He has four goals and 11 points in 12 games with the Edmonton Oilers in 2026-27.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Edmonton Oilers announced that forward Ryan Nugent-Hopkins will return to the lineup to face the Vegas Golden Knights in their game Tuesday night. He is expected to be on a line with Connor McDavid and Kasperi Kapanen . Nugent-Hopkins missed the last five games and has been out of the lineup since the Oilers’ 1-0 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs Nov. 14. The 33-year-old center has four goals and seven assists for 11 points in 12 games this season. Now in his 16th season, Nugent-Hopkins has 295 goals and 520 assists for 815 points in 1,043 regular-season games. Last January, he played his 1,000th career game . He’s also played in 102 career playoff games, where he’s scored 25 goals and recorded 61 assists for 86 points. He was part of Edmonton’s back-to-back Stanley Cup Final runs in 2024 and 2025. Nugent-Hopkins, a native of Burnaby, B.C., hit career highs in all offensive categories in 2022-23 when he recorded 37 goals and 67 assists for 104 points. He’s recorded at least 50 points in nine seasons. Taken with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft, Nugent-Hopkins spent two full seasons with the WHL’s Red Deer Rebels, where he scored 55 goals and recorded 116 assists for 166 points in 136 regular-season games. In his draft season, he recorded 31 goals and 75 assists for 106 points in 69 games. Internationally, he represented Canada at the 2013 World Junior Championship, where he scored four goals and 11 assists for 15 points. He also played for Team North America at the 2016 World Cup of Hockey, where he scored a goal and two assists for three points.

items.body: After a blockbuster trade pulled him out of Montreal, Michael Hage is embracing his new team. The University of Michigan junior said that he plans to sign with the Detroit Red Wings when his college season is done. “Yep,” he confirmed to Nicholas Cotsonika of NHL.com . “After, hopefully, we win a national championship.” Hage was part of the Dylan Larkin blockbuster that saw the Red Wings receive the 20-year-old along with forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, a first-round pick in 2027, a second-round pick in 2027, a fourth-round pick in 2028 and a first-round pick in 2029. Detroit also sent a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 third-round pick to Montreal. Hage was selected as the No. 21 pick in the 2024 draft by Montreal. items.title: Singer offers tearful apology for O Canada flub at Leafs-Islanders game in New York
items.body: A singer and former Broadway actress issued an emotional apology to Canadians after fumbling the lyrics to O Canada ahead of Monday night's matchup between the Toronto Maple Leafs and New York Islanders . Sarrah Strimel Bentley sang "We lend our hearts to thee" several times in place of "We stand on guard for thee." She also replaced "in" with "with" when she sang "True patriot love with all of us command." The singer took to social media shortly after to apologize and ask people to "be kind and show grace." Strimel Bentley said in an Instagram video that due to breast cancer she experiences menopause, which can be induced early by cancer treatments and can cause lapses in memory. She said she also experienced nerves singing an unfamiliar anthem in front of an audience of thousands. “I just wish that you would be a little easier on someone who is just a human being, and I'm sorry," Strimel Bentley said through tears. "Thank you for giving me grace. I love Canada. I stand on guard for thee." The Leafs referenced the lyric mishap in a post on X that shared video of defenceman Jack McCabe putting a puck in the Islanders' net for Toronto's first goal of the night. They would go on to beat the Islanders 4-2, ending a nine-game losing streak.

items.body: Conor Geekie will be out 4-5 months for the Tampa Bay Lightning after having shoulder surgery, the team announced on Tuesday. The forward, who had surgery on Monday and will begin rehab immediately, was placed on injured reserve on Nov. 17 and has missed the past three games. He last played in a 2-0 loss to the Detroit Red Wings on Nov. 14 when he had two shots on goal in 8:32 of ice time. Geekie has five points (one goal, four assists) in 20 games this season. Lightning coach Jon Cooper said he expects Geekie to return before the season ends. "It's in the best interest of his career," Cooper told the Lightning's website. "He's still a young kid so he should be able to come through this. I wouldn't, by any means, say his season is done. He will be back in March probably. We're hoping. It's just weird as it seems like this is ripping through the league. It's too bad because he made great strides this year. "I don't think this is going to be a step back for him. This will probably be a plus for him because he has been dealing with this. Now, when he can put it behind him, I think it will be good for him" In three NHL seasons, all with the Lightning, Geekie has 22 points (13 goals, nine assists) in 86 regular-season games and one assist in six Stanley Cup Playoff games. items.summary: In the midst of the second season under the CHL and NCAA's eligibility changes, WHL commissioner Dan Near is still pleased with where the league stands as a developmental ground for the next generation of NHL stars.
items.body: Nov 24, 2026 3:29 PM Published Nov 24, 2026 3:29 PM In the midst of the second season under the CHL and NCAA's eligibility changes, WHL commissioner Dan Near is still pleased with where the league stands as a developmental ground for the next generation of NHL stars. The NCAA's new eligibility rule has changed junior hockey in North America. The 2026-27 season is the second under the new rule, which now allows CHL players to play for colleges in the United States. Players have taken full advantage of this, as over 400 players who have suited up in either the WHL, OHL or QMJHL are currently playing Division I hockey. While teams across the CHL are losing high-end players earlier than expected, the new NCAA eligibility rule has positively affected recruitment. Players who had previously committed to the NCAA can now join CHL teams instead of playing in leagues such as the BCHL, AJHL or USHL. Even if these players are only in the league for one or two seasons, having access to this talent pool is something that excites WHL Commissioner Dan Near. items.body: Register Login Canadiens Recall Brett Berard, David Reinbacher By Gabriel Foley | at November 24, 2026 8:34 am The Montreal Canadiens have fortified their depth ahead of a three-game road trip through the Western Conference. Montreal recalled winger Brett Berard and defenseman David Reinbacher . The two will serve as the only extra skaters on a Canadiens roster facing multiple injuries. Forwards Josh Anderson , Chris Kreider , and Ivan Demidov are all on injured reserve, while defenseman Mike Matheson is also sidelined. None of the four injured players will join Montreal’s upcoming travel. Both Berard and Reinbacher have been a part of Montreal’s response to so many injuries. Berard played in his first three games with Montreal last week. He recorded one assist and two shots on goal across those appearances, before returning to the Laval Rocket for one game this weekend. Reinbacher made an appearance in the Canadiens’ lineup on Saturday and recorded a plus-two before also being reassigned for Laval’s Sunday matchup. Across the AHL season, Berard has racked up a productive 11 points in 18 games. He is one of many cylinders firing in the Laval offense, improving on a dip in minor-league scoring through his final two years in the New York Rangers’ organization. Berard scored 48 points in 71 games of his rookie AHL season but followed that with 45 points in 71 games across the next two years. Through those appearances, he also played in 48 games with the Rangers, marked by 10 points, 14 penalty minutes, and a minus-seven. Reinbacher has a tamer seven points, plus-eight, and 22 penalty minutes in 16 AHL games this season. The former fifth-overall pick continues to serve as a focal point of the Rockets’ lineup, while notching his second season with a pair of NHL appearances.

items.body: The Montreal Canadiens recalled the pair from the AHL's Laval Rocket, the team announced Tuesday. The move comes just two days after the Habs sent both players down — and one day after the team introduced new star centre Dylan Larkin after a trade from the Detroit Red Wings. Both Berard and Reinbacher appeared in Saturday's 4-3 loss to the Philadelphia Flyers. Berard played 7:10 in the defeat but notched his first assist at the NHL level since the 2024-25 season. The 24-year-old has played three games this season. Since making his NHL debut in the 2024-25 season, the Providence, R.I., native has six goals and five assists in 51 games. Reinbacher, meanwhile, was playing in only his second game of the year against Philadelphia. Though he finished without a point — and has yet to record one this season — he had 10 minutes of ice time and three shots on goal. The fifth-overall pick has made only four appearances, recording one point at the NHL level since being drafted in 2023. items.summary: Frost was hit hard by Ottawa’s Tyler Kleven early in the second period on Monday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Calgary Flames center Morgan Frost left Monday’s game against the Ottawa Senators during the second period after sustaining an upper-body injury. Frost, 27, was visibly shaken up after taking a hard hit from Senators defenseman Tyler Kleven early in the middle frame. After heading down the tunnel toward the Flames’ dressing room, Frost briefly returned and played a couple more shifts before leaving the game for good. Kleven was not penalized for the hit, but Flames winger Joel Farabee was assessed two roughing penalties for his role in the post-whistle scrum; Ottawa’s Ridly Greig was also called for roughing on the play. Frost logged 8:53 of ice time, took one shot on goal, and finished with a minus-one rating across 10 shifts before exiting Monday’s game. The Flames ultimately lost the game by a 2-1 final score. Through 25 games with the Flames this season, Frost has collected five goals and 14 points. The Aurora, Ont. product is under contract with the Flames at a $4.375 million contract through the end of 2026-27, at which point he can become an unrestricted free agent. The Flames acquired Frost and Farabee together from the Philadelphia Flyers midway through the 2024-25 season. Frost set a new career high with 22 goals in 82 games with the Flames in 2025-26; he tied Mikael Backlund for second on the team with 43 points. The Flyers originally selected Frost in the first round (No. 27 overall) of the 2017 NHL Draft. The 6’0″ center followed up a strong junior career with the OHL’s Soo Greyhounds by turning pro within the Flyers organization in 2019-20, appearing in his first 20 NHL games with the club that year. In 417 career NHL games over parts of eight seasons split between the Flyers and Flames, Frost has collected 80 goals and 204 points.

items.summary: Palmieri took an awkward fall during the second period on Tuesday night against the Maple Leafs.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Not the greatest sight on Long Island. During a matchup between the New York Islanders and Toronto Maple Leafs , Islanders forward Kyle Palmieri left the game prematurely due to a lower-body injury. The veteran center was hurt several minutes into the second period. While trying to tie up Maple Leafs forward Easton Cowan, Palmieri started to lose his balance before awkwardly colliding with an also-falling Nick Paul, with Palmieri crashing into the Islanders’ net. The 35-year-old was able to return to the bench, but he eventually went down the tunnel into the Isles’ dressing room. The team confirmed once the third period began that Palmieri wouldn’t be coming back to the game. Palmieri logged a season-low 8:12 of ice time across nine shifts. The Islanders were up 2-0 on the Leafs before Palmieri’s injury. However, the Isles squandered the lead, as Toronto scored four unanswered goals to pick up the win, ending the Leafs’ nine-game losing streak. Islanders head coach Pete DeBoer didn’t have an update on Palmieri following the contest. The Smithtown, N.Y. native had appeared in each of the team’s first 23 games of the 2026-27 season. He has notched four goals and five assists for nine points, with a plus/minus of +2 while averaging 16:07 of ice time per game. Palmieri is in the second and final season of his two-year contract extension, which he signed in May 2025. The deal has a cap hit of $4.75 million, with a modified no-trade clause where the player submits a 16-team no-trade list. Despite the loss, the Islanders (11-7-5) remain third in the Metropolitan Division, 12 points back of the first-place Carolina Hurricanes . items.title: Ullmark leads Senators to win over Flames
items.summary: Linus Ullmark continued his impressive start to the season on Monday, making 34 saves to lead the Ottawa Senators to a 2-1 victory over the Calgary Flames.
items.body: Linus Ullmark continued his impressive start to the season on Monday, making 34 saves to lead the Ottawa Senators to a 2-1 victory over the Calgary Flames. Michael Amadio and Shane Pinto each scored, allowing Ottawa (16-6-3) to close out its three-game homestand with a 2-0-1 record. Matt Coronato scored the lone goal for the Flames (10-13-2), who were playing the first of a five-game Eastern road trip. Devin Cooley, who continues to look for his first road win of the season (0-4-0) was busy, stopping 29 of 31 shots. The Flames made it a one-goal game, 2-1, when Coronato scored a third-period power-play goal beating Ullmark glove side. The Flames found themselves short-handed early in the second after Ottawa’s Tyler Kleven caught Morgan Frost with a hard bodycheck that sent the Calgary forward to the ice. The hit was reviewed but no penalty was assessed. Joel Farabee was instead handed a double minor for roughing after coming to Frost’s defence, while Ottawa’s Ridly Greig received a roughing minor. With 48 seconds remaining in the period the Senators had a scare when Tim Stutzle hit the goalpost and grabbed his left knee. The Senators leading scorer went right to the dressing room but was back on the ice for the third. Amadio opened the scoring midway through the period when he intercepted the puck out front, made a move to pull Cooley and beat him glove side. Just over five minutes later Pinto stepped into the faceoff circle and snapped a shot past Cooley for his 10th of the season. Cooley faced a flurry of shots in the early parts of the period and made four straight saves to keep the Senators at bay. With Monday’s win the Senators matched their longest point streak, nine games (7-0-2), since a run in 2014-15.

The 21-year-old center was injured in the Blackhawks’ 6-3 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Nov. 17. He was set to take a face-off against Maple Leafs forward Nick Paul 54 seconds into the third period when, as Bedard put his stick on the ice, Paul’s stick made contact with Bedard’s right hand. The Blackhawks captain yelled out in pain and immediately went to the locker room. Bedard has 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) in 15 games this season, tied for the Blackhawks lead with forward Roman Kantserov (13 goals, five assists). Bedard scored his seventh goal of the season at 18:51 of the second period on Tuesday, giving the Blackhawks a 3-2 lead. “Obviously we’re thinking about him,” forward Patrick Kane said Thursday. “I think he knows how big of a piece he is to this team, what he means to the organization. Entertainment value, right, for fans and for the League and what he’s able to provide to the game. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images The Chicago Blackhawks have announced that Connor Bedard will miss approximately four months following successful shoulder surgery this week. Bedard injured his right shoulder following a faceoff in a game against the Toronto Maple Leafs last week. The Blackhawks have since placed Bedard on injured reserve. The 21-year-old had surgery on that very same right shoulder on July 8, and was forced to miss the Blackhawks’ first six game this season while in recovery. The British Columbia native is in his fourth NHL season since being drafted first overall in 2023. As a rookie in the 2023-24 season, he notched 22 goals and 39 assists for 61 points in 68 games en route to winning the Calder Trophy. His sophomore season of 2024-25 saw him register 23 goals and 44 assists for 67 assists in all 82 games. He had the best year of his career last season, putting up 30 goals and 45 assists for 75 points in 69 games. Bedard is in the first season of a five-year, $75 million contract with the Blackhawks. The Blackhawks sit dead last in the Central Division with a record of 8-14-2, giving them 18 points through 24 games. That’s third last in the Western Conference and fourth last in the league overall. Rookie Roman Kantserov currently shares the team lead in points with Bedard with 13 goals and 18 points in 24 games. With Bedard out, continued emphasis will be placed on Patrick Kane (17) and Frank Nazar (16) to help contribute offensively. Frost was checked into the boards in the Ottawa end by Kleven just a little over five minutes into the period and stayed down on the ice in visible pain while teammate Joel Farabee came to his defence. Officials reviewed the hit, but determined that Kleven would not be penalized on the play. Farabee received four minutes, and Senators forward Ridly Greig received two for roughing. Frost would eventually skate off under his own power before going to the Flames' locker room. He did return for a pair of shifts later in the frame, but went back down the tunnel before being ruled out. items.body: Connor Bedard will not be returning to the ice until early spring. Bedard will be out for four months after undergoing successful shoulder surgery, the Chicago Blackhawks announced on Monday. Bedard got hurt on a face-off early in the third period against the Toronto Maple Leafs last Tuesday. The 21-year-old centre slammed his stick on the ice and held his right arm in front of him as he made his way to the locker room. Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson told reporters Saturday that Bedard would undergo right shoulder surgery after exiting that win over the Maple Leafs. Chicago placed Bedard on the injured reserve Sunday and recalled forward Dominic Toninato in a corresponding move. Bedard has a history of shoulder issues. He missed extended time last season with a right shoulder injury and underwent surgery on his left shoulder during the off-season. Bedard missed the Blackhawks' first five games of the season rehabilitating that injury. The 2023-24 Rookie of the Year, Bedard had 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) in 15 games since returning. items.body: Register Login Red Wings Place Sheldon Dries On Waivers By Brennan McClain | at November 23, 2026 2:02 pm The Detroit Red Wings had one too many forwards on the roster after acquiring Kirby Dach from the Montreal Canadiens last night as part of the return package for Dylan Larkin . To thin out the forward corps, the Red Wings have placed Sheldon Dries on waivers, per Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman . Dries, 32, has already spent more time with Detroit than he expected this year. After spending most of his first two years in the Red Wings organization with the Grand Rapids Griffins in the AHL, Dries inked a two-year, $1.75MM extension with Detroit last February. Primarily an injury replacement, Dries went scoreless in five games for the Red Wings last season. He was exceptional in the AHL, registering 23 goals and 45 points in 57 games with a +20 rating. Unlike last season, Dries has played for the Red Wings more often than not. Since Detroit suspended Larkin without pay, Dries has held down a consistent role in the Red Wings’ lineup. Still, he hasn’t been that productive, registering only one assist in 16 games while averaging 10:06 of ice time per game. In his brief time with the Griffins this season, Dries has scored five goals and eight points in games with a +4 rating. Still, although he hasn’t been as offensively fruitful as he has been in the AHL, Dries has found other ways to contribute. Before being placed on waivers, Dries was fifth on the team in hits (34), and he has held his own defensively, maintaining a 90.7% on-ice SV%, good for 11th on the team.

items.body: Defenseman will miss second straight game against Sharks on Monday VANCOUVER -- Quinn Hughes was placed on injured reserve with an undisclosed injury and will miss the conclusion of the Minnesota Wild's three-game road trip at the San Jose Sharks on Monday (10 p.m. ET; Wild+, MINNHL, NBCSCA, SN360, SN). The defenseman was being further evaluated after he left a 4-1 win at the Calgary Flames on Thursday following a hit from Flames forward Adam Klapka at 9:57 of the third period. Wild coach John Hynes did not have an update after the game and declined to specify the nature of the injury prior to a 4-3 shootout loss at the Vancouver Canucks on Saturday, but a concussion has been ruled out. “He's not going to play on the trip, so he's going to go back to Minny and get reevaluated now and we’ll have some more info,” Hynes said before the game. Hughes has 21 points (six goals, 15 assists) during a NHL career high 13 -game point streak (including a goal and an assist Thursday) that set a Wild record for defensemen. Hughes ranks second among NHL defensemen with 34 points (eight goals, 26 assists) in 24 games. He leads all skaters in time on ice per game (27:49) and is plus-15. “There's not a lot of people that can replace what he does on a nightly basis, offensively, defensively, the way he controls the game, so you'll miss that,” Wild forward Nick Foligno said of Hughes. “But we’ve got so much confidence in the guys in this room that will make up for it and pick up the slack like he does when other guys are out.” Saturday would have been Hughes’ second trip back to Vancouver since he was traded to Minnesota on Dec. 12, 2025. The 27-year-old was booed in his first game back on Oct. 25, a 4-2 win for the Wild, in which he had a goal and an assist, including his 500th NHL point.

His 33-save performance in a 1-0 win over Pittsburgh on Sunday marked his league-leading fifth shutout of the season and the 21st of his career. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The leadership group in one of the Professional Women’s Hockey League’s newest teams has been revealed. On Monday, the Hamilton Havoc announced that forward Brianne Jenner has been named the franchise’s first captain. Fellow forwards Alina Muller and Emily Clark were also named alternates for the 2026-27 season. All three players were foundational signings for the new organization in Southern Ontario, signed by the Havoc during Phase 2 of the PWHL Expansion Player Distribution Process. Jenner, who served as captain of the Ottawa Charge during the league’s first three years of operation, admitted how excited she is to be leading the new team in Hamilton. “I’m really looking forward to leading our team and the city of Hamilton as captain,” Jenner said in a release. “I’m incredibly grateful for this opportunity. Having grown up in nearby Oakville, I understand what hockey means to this community and the passion that exists throughout the region. We have a wonderful opportunity ahead of us in a great hockey city, and I’m excited to help build something new and meaningful for the community. I’m proud to be a part of it and look forward to what we can accomplish together.” Jenner is one of the most decorated players of her generation. Having been a member of the Canadian National Team since the 2012 IIHF Women’s World Championship, the Oakville, Ont. native has won gold at the Women’s Worlds four times, with two gold medals at the Winter Olympics. He will provide extra depth after Martin Pospisil was injured in Saturday’s loss to the Chicago Blackhawks. Calgary seemed prepared for Morton’s recall, with the centerman being held out of the Wranglers’ Sunday matchup. Morton will now receive his first call-up of the season, and his first since signing a one-year extension with Calgary over the summer. The 27 year old has scored six points, eight penalty minutes, and a minus-three in 20 games with the Wranglers this season. He has been a go-to depth forward through the last two seasons – though that role has only resulted in Morton making four NHL appearances. He’s marked those games with one goal and 10 penalty minutes. Morton has otherwise been productive in the minor-league. He reached a career-high 45 points in 70 games of the 2024-25 season, good for the fifth-most points on the Wranglers that season. He repeated that standing last season, notching 38 points in 68 games to rank fifth again. The Flames will have Morton as an option for Monday’s matchup against the Ottawa Senators. They will decide between Morton and Brennan Othmann to fill the hole left open by Pospisil. Othmann has yet to score through seven games this season. He notched two points in as many games with Calgary last season, after joining the team via trade ahead of the 2026 Trade Deadline. Monday’s matchup could represent another chance to help Othmann find his groove. If not, Calgary will have the gritty Morton to help replace Pospisil’s physical presence.

On Saturday night, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman informed fans that the Wings were broadening their approach regarding the desired return for Dylan Larkin . Initially, Detroit was steadfast in its belief that any Larkin swap must return a similar player who could step right into the lineup. But with this season slipping away fast, interim GM Shawn Horcoff altered his ask and began looking at pitches centred around top-level prospects. The Habs were long seen — from a pure hockey standpoint — as a fantastic fit for Larkin. This is Hage’s third season playing just down the road from Detroit with the Michigan Wolverines, who have a great shot at the national championship this year. Hage is joined on the Wolverines by Will Horcoff, son of the suit who just acquired him for the Wings.
